stories.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November, with a seafarer killed in a Gulf tanker attack and a VLCC struck. Separately, US forces fired on and disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday as it tried to breach the US blockade of Iranian ports.
stories.why_it_matters: Crew fatalities, hull strikes and armed blockade enforcement raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting tanker earnings.
stories.latest: US Central Command says an American military aircraft disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday, the first such action in a month; trade press reports soaring tanker rates are deepening discounts on heavy crude grades.

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts now describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
stories.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.
stories.latest: ARACON 26 delegates were told that 25% of the internationally trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

stories.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
stories.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
stories.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.
stories.latest: The union agreed to continue negotiations for two more weeks, deferring the strike threat again without resolving it.
sources: LA Port Strike Threat Deferred Again As Labor Talks Drag On

stories.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
stories.what: Strait of Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG movements even as VLCC traffic declined. Red Sea traffic also rose and Arabian Gulf waiting remains elevated.
stories.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
sources: Seafarer fatality in Gulf tanker attack, VLCC struck in Hormuz

stories.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
stories.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Webinar: Navigating the danger zone: How to protect your fleet from GPS attacks

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
sources: Soaring Freight Rates Give US Refiners Edge As Crude Discounts Widen
